https://www.koreaherald.com/article/1082.text: Hungary to shut down sole nuclear plant as Danube falls to record low, PM says Published : Aug. 2, 2026 - 12:26:12 Add The Korea Herald on Google Link copied! Paks Nuclear Power Plant with the partially dried-up Danube riverbed in Dunaszentbenedek, Hungary, Friday (Reuters-Yonhap) BUDAPEST, Hungary (Reuters) -- Hungary will power down its Paks nuclear power plant for the first time in nearly half a ‌century, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said Saturday, as water levels on the Danube River the plant uses as a coolant have plumbed record lows. The shutdown comes as large parts of Europe have been hit by prolonged heat and drought, driving river levels lower and raising concerns about water supplies, shipping and power generation. Falls ⁠in water levels amid a lack of rain have also disrupted shipping and tourism in Hungary and triggered water-use restrictions in more than 100 cities and villages, including on the outskirts of Budapest, based on government records. The energy crisis could also hit the wider economy, which grew less ⁠than forecast in the second quarter following a three-year stretch of stagnation. "Due to a further decline in the Danube's water level, the second-to-last generating unit at the Paks nuclear power plant will be shut down at 1:30 a.m.," Magyar said in ​a Facebook post. "As a result, the plant is now producing only 240 megawatts (of electricity), and tomorrow (on Sunday), for the first ‌time in 44 years, it will be completely shut down." Hungary's water authority was projecting the water level on the Danube River, which flows from ‌Germany to the Black ‌Sea, to decline further in the next days. Hungary's northern neighbor Slovakia offered help, with Prime Minister Robert Fico ‌describing the situation as an unprecedented energy crisis caused by the looming ​shutdown of Hungary's only nuclear power plant. "I am closely monitoring the energy crisis in Hungary and express our full solidarity with our neighbour, along with our readiness ⁠to help," Fico said in a Facebook post, adding nuclear plants in Slovakia were operating at their planned capacity. The crisis could cost Hungary 100 billion to 200 billion forints ($315 million to $630 million) due to the surging price of imported electricity, Mark Radnai, vice chairman of Magyar's Tisza party, ⁠said on Facebook. Magyar, ​who has warned that Paks could remain ⁠idled for weeks, said his cabinet would issue a decree seeking voluntary power demand cuts from large users in addition to 240 MW of cuts already committed. Penalties ​would apply if those targets were missed. The decree would also allow grid operator MAVIR to seek mandatory reductions in power consumption from big users and temporarily cut certain large consumers off the grid, if needed. "Households will be the last in the chain of restrictions," Magyar ⁠said. Earlier Saturday, engineers restored 360 MW of power output lost due to ⁠a malfunction at ⁠Hungary's largest gas-fired ‌power plant in Szazhalombatta, but Magyar said additional measures were needed to ease the load on the power grid. From Monday, rail cargo services will be stopped between 3 p.m. to 8 p.m. to reduce power demand. The government will also order public sector staff to work from home for the first ​three days of this week and ask companies to follow suit wherever possible. Floodlights on Hungarian public buildings and non-essential lighting will also be switched off, Magyar said, adding that record-low water levels have also triggered water consumption restrictions in the worst-hit areas. "Each drop of water counts," he said. good 0 sad 0 angry 0 recommended 0 More from Headlines Lee underscores peace with N. https://www.dw.com/en/indonesia-rescuers.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MWBE The Virgo Transport 8 ferry ran into bad weather in Indonesia while sailing from Java to Borneo Image: Infuz/AFP Advertisement An Indonesian passenger ship carrying 243 people sank in the Java Sea on Sunday after it was hit by bad weather, local authorities said. Officials said six people had died, while 107 were brought to safety and some 130 passengers were still missing. "We have carried out efforts to search for victims to the fullest extent. There were passengers who ... had already been successfully evacuated by the units at the scene," I Putu Sudayana, head of the Banjarmasin Search and Rescue Office, told reporters. The Virgo Transport 8 was traveling from Indonesia's second-largest city of Surabaya to Banjarmasin, the capital of South Kalimantan province on Borneo island. It departed on Saturday at 10:13 a.m. local time (0330 UTC), but the ship's operator lost contact with the vessel early Sunday amid bad weather. It was scheduled to arrive in Banjarmasin at about 2 p.m. local time on (0700 UTC) Sunday. Over 100 people have been rescued during ongoing search and rescue operations Image: Infuz/AFP Search operation underway Search and rescue teams launched an operation after the operator alerted authorities. Ships and a helicopter were deployed to the vessel's last known location. "The ship's operator reported the incident to authorities after receiving information that the vessel had encountered bad weather," Sudayana said in an earlier video briefing. The ship's last known position was in the Java Sea, roughly 148 kilometers (92 miles) from a pier in Banjarmasin, according to the Associated Press. Sudayana added that authorities were mobilizing all available personnel and equipment given the large number of people aboard. The agency was coordinating with maritime authorities while closely monitoring weather conditions in the area, he said. Indonesia, a nation of roughly 17,000 islands, relies heavily on ferries for transportation, with sea travel often cheaper and more accessible than flying. But safety enforcement across the country's maritime sector has been inconsistent, contributing to a comparatively high rate of accidents. https://www.theyeshivaworld.com/news/isr.text: PEGASUS CONTROVERSY: Poland’s Tusk Claims Spyware Exposed Sensitive Data to Israel; Former Anti-Corruption Chief Denies It October 12, 2026 1:30 pm No Comments Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has sparked a political dispute by claiming that the previous government’s use of Pegasus spyware exposed sensitive security and civilian information to Israeli hands. A former senior Polish official rejected the accusation, insisting that Israeli parties had no access to surveillance data. Tusk said Poland’s Internal Security Agency had confirmed the exposure. He accused the previous government of spending more than 30 million zlotys from a fund intended to assist crime victims to purchase the surveillance system developed by Israeli company NSO Group. According to Tusk, Polish security services lacked effective control over the technology they purchased. He claimed the system transmitted information concerning Polish citizens, opposition leaders and independent prosecutors, while control over that information effectively remained with the Israeli company. He characterized the arrangement as “betrayal.” The accusations drew a sharp response from right-wing journalist and online commentator Paweł Rybicki, who accused Tusk of using anti-Jewish rhetoric for political gain. Rybicki linked the remarks to what he described as a significant electoral defeat for Tusk’s party in Krakow, arguing that the prime minister was attempting to exploit antisemitic sentiment to strengthen his political position. Separately, the former head of Poland’s Central Anti-Corruption Bureau, known as the CBA, firmly denied Tusk’s account and accused him of misleading the public. The former official said Pegasus had been operated legally and under the bureau’s regulatory framework, with Polish security services retaining exclusive control over both the system and the information collected. “The Israeli side was not exposed to data concerning surveillance targets or the information obtained,” he said. Disclaimer Links PAGES on NUCLEAR ISSUES Zelensky wants another $175bn for 2027: Europe doesn’t have it . Zelensky is now talking about a rise from roughly $100 billion to $155 billion next year. The EU is already cutting education and social programmes to fund the present level Meanwhile Ukraine’s own economy is already in advanced collapse. A conversation with Ben Aris of BNE Intellinews Ian Proud , Nov 06, 2026 , https://thepeacemonger.substack.com/p/zelensky-wants-another-175bn-for?utm_source=post-email-title&publication_id=3221990&post_id=223752719&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1ise1&triedRedirect=true&utm_medium=email Zelensky’s latest demand for yet more money collides with two hard realities: Europe does not have it, and Russia continues to outproduce the West in the munitions that decide late-stage industrial wars. ben aris of bne IntelliNews, whose recent analysis of defence production costs cuts should provide a cold shower to those who cling to the hope that the arithmetic of war will eventually turn in Ukraine’s favour. Nominal Russian defence spending is about $210 billion against America’s near-trillion. On purchasing-power terms the gap narrows to roughly 60 per cent. Once you price the actual outputs—$1,000 for a Russian 155 mm shell versus $4,000 for its American counterpart—the effective capacity closes further. Artillery, missiles and especially drones are where the disparity bites. Russia has scaled cheap, mass-produced systems; the West still fields small numbers of expensive platforms such as the MQ-9 Reaper at $30 million apiece. Trump’s instruction to double interceptor production has been met with timelines stretching to 2030. Ukraine cannot wait that long. Europe’s fiscal position makes the gap unbridgeable in the short term. Zelensky is now talking about a rise from roughly $100 billion to $155 billion next year. The EU is already cutting education and social programmes to fund the present level; demonstrations in Berlin are the visible result. Debt ratios in France, Italy and the UK leave little room for further borrowing, and Germany’s relative strength won’t help it convince and increasingly anti-war public. Globalisation has hollowed out the industrial base that would be needed for a rapid wartime surge to bring the nations of Europe on a par with Russia. Turning car plants into tank factories smacks of panic production. Meanwhile Ukraine’s own economy is already in advanced collapse. Metals production, a pre-war export mainstay, has fallen to zero. Grain shipments through Odessa are repeatedly interrupted, with stocks rotting in fields and silos. The power grid is being systematically dismantled at the substation level; Kyiv has gone dark and three remaining nuclear plants cannot feed a grid whose connections are being destroyed. Debt has crossed 100 per cent of GDP. Trade deficits with the EU have widened sharply as tariff exemptions lapsed and weapons purchases were added to the import bill. Demographics are worse still: millions of women and children have left and show little incentive to return to a ruined economy and a generation of missing men. These facts render the usual political slogans—“Ukraine must win,” “EU membership is the destination”—impractical. Full membership of the EU for Ukraine will never happen precisely because it would expose the Common Agricultural Policy to Ukrainian volumes that, on present rules, could cost the EU budget on the order of $186 billion a year. That is far more than the yearly sums tipped into the proxy-war effort thus far. As I have said many times, that helps to explain why the Eurocrats keeping kicking the war can down the road. Net recipients of EU budget support such as Poland and Hungary would become net contributors and would veto. On which, I wrote about this over two years ago for Responsible Statecraft …. A watered-down association agreement is the more realistic commercial outcome for Ukraine; the ability to trade with all nations including Russia, neutrality and limited armed forces remain the political terms Moscow has repeated since 2022. Late-stage wars are settled by who can put more metal in the air and on the ground. Russia has been doing that since the first months; the West’s production response has a multi-year lag built in. Europe’s public finances and Ukraine’s residual economy cannot wait that long. The rational course is therefore a negotiated settlement that freezes the line, limits force levels and restores trade, before the remaining productive capacity and population base of Ukraine disappear entirely. The alternative is a rump state whose reconstruction costs will still fall, in large part, on the same European treasuries that are already running out of money. https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/11/23/ukra.text: Az Ukrán Biztonsági Szolgálat (SZBU) megerősítette, hogy tengeri drónokat vetett be két orosz hajó ellen Líbia partjainál – írja a Guardian . A Bengázi haditengerészeti támaszpontjánál szombaton dróntámadással megrongált orosz hadihajó hétfőn süllyedt el , miközben vasárnap este egy másik, máltai zászló alatt közlekedő teherhajót is támadás ért a kelet-líbiai partoknál. Műholdfelvételek alapján a korábban megtámadott hajó a Merkury nevű orosz korvett volt. Az SZBU hétfői közlése szerint a támadások során összesen hét ukrán gyártmányú tengeri drónt vetettek be. „Az ukrán védelmi erők ismét bebizonyították, hogy az orosz haditengerészetnek és logisztikai hálózatainak nincsenek biztonságos útvonalai, még a Fekete-tengertől jóval távolabb sem” – írta az SZBU. A Líbia partjainál végrehajtott támadásokat Volodimir Zelenszkij ukrán elnök az X-en hétfő reggel „példamutató ukrán műveletként” jellemezte. Az ukrán elnök a Merkuryról azt írta, az „az egyik legújabb hajójuk, amelyet 2023-ban, a teljes körű háború idején állítottak hadrendbe”. A másikat, az MV ANGARA orosz szárazáru-szállító hajót az oroszok Zelenszkij szerint fegyverszállításra használták. A múlt héten megrongált kercsi hídhoz hasonlóan a Merkury elsüllyesztése is presztízsveszteség Vlagyimir Putyin számára. Az orosz elnök 2019-ben személyesen is meglátogatta a szentpétervári hajógyárat, ahol a hajót építették, a 2023-as Haditengerészeti Napon tartott beszédében pedig név szerint említette a korvettet mint bizonyítékot arra, hogy Oroszország „következetesen erősíti flottájának erejét”. Moammer Kadhafi egykori líbiai vezető megbuktatása óta Líbia különböző milíciák által ellenőrzött területekre szakadt, és jelenleg két rivális kormány között oszlik meg. A keleti, Nemzeti Stabilitási Kormány (GNS) közölte, hogy az orosz hajó egy meglévő tengeri megállapodás keretében használta a bengázi kikötőt. Líbia nemzetközileg elismert tripoli kormánya – a Nemzeti Egység Kormánya (GNU) – az esetre reagálva felhívta rá a figyelmet, hogy nem jó döntés idegen erőket fogadni a líbiai létesítményekben. Az ENSZ líbiai missziója (UNSMIL) „súlyos aggodalmának” adott hangot az események miatt, és az incidensek azonnali, független és átlátható kivizsgálását sürgette. Szombaton dróntámadás ért egy orosz teherhajót a Balti-tengeren is. A kalinyingrádi exklávéba tartó, 121 méteres Sparta II nevű hajó az orosz Gogland-szigettől nyugatra, nemzetközi vizeken sérült meg, majd később finn felségvizekre sodródott. A finn hatóságok szerint a támadás mögött feltehetően Ukrajna állt. Petteri Orpo finn miniszterelnök hangsúlyozta, hogy a háború már a szomszédos területekre is átterjed, de Ukrajnának joga van védekezni az agresszor ellen. A Kreml hétfőn azzal vádolta Ukrajnát, hogy „terrorista tevékenységet” folytat a Balti-tengeren, és kijelentette, reméli, a balti-tengeri államok befolyásukat latba vetve figyelmeztetik Kijevet a hasonló gyakorlatok ellen.
